faqs.a: It depends on your margins and industry. As a rough rule, 2x is the minimum most businesses accept, 4x is strong, and anything above that is excellent. A business with 90% margins can thrive at 1.5x, while one with 20% margins needs much more.

ROAS divides revenue by ad spend only. ROI divides profit by total investment, including every cost. A campaign can have a great ROAS and still lose money overall if the product costs and overhead are high.
faqs.q: What is the difference between ROAS and ROI?

faqs.a: ROAS itself cannot be negative because revenue and spend are both zero or positive. The closest concept is a ROAS below 1.0, which means you are losing money on the ads.

The standard definition uses gross revenue. If you want a stricter view, subtract your cost of goods sold from revenue first and you get something closer to a profit-based ROAS, which many advertisers call POAS.
faqs.q: Should I use revenue or profit in the ROAS formula?

faqs.a: Ad auctions, seasonality, creative fatigue, and audience saturation all move ROAS. Compare the same campaign to its own history rather than to other advertisers, and give changes at least a week to settle.
faqs.q: Why does my ROAS change over time?

faqs.a: Only if the ads serve another purpose, like acquiring customers who buy again later. On the ads alone, 1.0 means break-even before any other cost, so it is a loss in practice.

roas-calculator.formula:
ROAS = Revenue / Ad spend
ROAS % = (Revenue / Ad spend) x 100
Gross profit = Revenue - Ad spend
Profit per unit of spend = (Revenue - Ad spend) / Ad spend
Example: 2,500 / 500 = 5.0 -> 500%.

keyFacts: ROAS (Return on Ad Spend) = revenue generated / advertising cost.
A ROAS of 1.0 is break-even on ad spend. Below 1.0 loses money, above 1.0 makes money.
ROAS is not the same as ROI. ROI includes all costs; ROAS only looks at the ad cost.
Good ROAS benchmarks vary wildly: 2x may be excellent in competitive retail and weak in digital products.
ROAS ignores product cost, shipping, taxes, and salaries - it only judges the ads, not the business.

roas-calculator.workedExample:
Ad spend 500, revenue 2,500:
1. ROAS = 2,500 / 500 = 5.0.
2. ROAS % = 5.0 x 100 = 500%.
3. Gross profit = 2,500 - 500 = 2,000.
4. Profit per unit of spend = 2,000 / 500 = 4.0.
